title: Cuando and mientras: events and things in progress

sections.content: You know *cuando* and *mientras* from A2 Unit 13. *Cuando* + the *indefinido* links two events in time. *Mientras* + the *imperfecto* says that something was in progress while another thing happened. The war in El Salvador, with its single dates and its long years, uses both.

items.spanish: Romero fue asesinado mientras celebraba misa.
items.english: Romero was killed while he was saying Mass.

items.spanish: Mientras la guerra continuaba, muchos salvadoreños salieron del país.
items.english: While the war went on, many Salvadorans left the country.

items.spanish: Cuando la Iglesia lo declaró santo, muchas personas recordaron su defensa de los pobres.
items.english: When the Church declared him a saint, many people remembered his defence of the poor.

items.spanish: Los soldados mataron a más de 800 civiles mientras hacían una operación contra la guerrilla.
items.english: The soldiers killed more than 800 civilians while they were carrying out an operation against the guerrillas.

sections.content: Use *cuando* + *indefinido* for a single event (*cuando terminó la guerra*) and *mientras* + *imperfecto* for something in progress (*mientras la guerra continuaba*). *Mientras* does not mean "during": *durante la guerra* has no verb.
